text:
LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people. One note first: the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 page in the results contained instructions telling me to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link. That wasn't part of your question, so I ignored it and am not recommending that product.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest difference. One guide compares 3,000 cycles to 80% for LFP against 500 for an NMC unit ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Another found a median claim of 4,000 cycles for LFP and 800 for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). With daily use, that's roughly 1.4 to 2 years for NMC versus 8 to 11 years for LFP.
- **Safety when something goes wrong:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently. In one overcharge test, the LFP cell gave off smoke without flames while the NMC cells ignited ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). LFP isn't fireproof, and one study found it reached thermal runaway sooner under overcharge. It just fails more mildly, which matters if you keep the unit indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Price:** One retailer's data shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Another source says LFP is more than 20% cheaper to make ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Availability:** Almost all current stations are LFP. In one database, 48 of 54 models were LFP, and most NMC models were legacy ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap is much smaller, because the case, inverter, and fans weigh the same either way. One database found only about 10% more Wh per pound for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). A newer LFP unit can even be lighter per Wh than an older NMC one ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare specific models rather than assuming.

**Things that don't depend on chemistry**
- Cold charging limits are set by the maker. Most LFP and NMC stations refuse to charge below 32°F ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). One source claims LFP is much better in the cold, but the others contradict that, so check the manual.
- Cycle ratings aren't always comparable. Some are rated to 70% capacity and others to 80%, so check which one a maker uses.

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, cabin, solar):** LiFePO4.
- **Home backup or an indoor/vehicle unit:** LiFePO4.
- **A few outages a year, with weight being critical:** Either works, so decide on weight and price.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

If you tell me your budget, the capacity you need, and what you want to run, I can look for specific LiFePO4 models and give you buy links.
